subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should OpenClaw broaden `api.runtime.gateway.request` beyond bundled/trusted official plugins to support third-party inter-plugin Gateway calls, or keep third-party plugins on a different capability/service contract?
rationale: The remaining choice changes the public Plugin SDK and Gateway authorization boundary, and automation cannot safely choose whether arbitrary external plugins may invoke method-string Gateway RPCs.

options.title: Design an explicit external-plugin contract
options.body: Add a documented third-party inter-plugin or capability API with caller attribution, permission checks, allowed methods or typed services, and contract tests.

options.title: Keep the trusted-only Gateway request boundary
options.body: Treat `api.runtime.gateway.request` as an official-plugin-only surface and ask third-party plugins to use another explicit service/capability mechanism.

options.title: Allow raw method-string dispatch broadly
options.body: Expose generic Gateway method calls to external plugins, accepting a larger compatibility and authorization surface.

recommendation.title: Design an explicit external-plugin contract
recommendation.body: Add a documented third-party inter-plugin or capability API with caller attribution, permission checks, allowed methods or typed services, and contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a Plugin SDK and Gateway security-boundary product decision rather than a mechanical follow-up to the partial implementation.
